title: Mediation Analysis with a Mediator Censored below an Assay Detection Limit
banked_reason: D0.5.G: incremental below field; moving-diagonal counterexample invalidates causal identification in the declared class; only the statistical-functional occupancy result survives
gap_reasons: the advertised causal frontier fails for the full-law class literally defined
lem:mediation-identification evaluates fixed-m conditional expectations on the random diagonal M=m, which pointwise exchangeability does not justify
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the occupancy estimator, variance certificate, assay bump lower bound, and adaptive interval result for the statistical functional ∫μ₁ f₀. D0.5 found that the declared pointwise mediator exchangeability does not identify this functional with the independent-intervention causal target; a binary moving-diagonal construction has identical observed laws but different causal means. The causal frontier is therefore unsound in this class. An independent structural-noise model would change the load-bearing class and needs a fresh novelty review; the surviving statistical result was graded incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: A randomized study observes the binary outcome for every participant but only a censoring flag when the continuous mediator lies below a public assay limit. For every fixed \(\beta\in(1/4,1]\), minimax expected absolute error and minimum worst-case expected length of a \(90\%\)-honest connected interval both have order \(n^{-1/2}+\lambda^{2\beta+1}\) over the bespoke positive H\"older benchmark, uniformly in sample size and assay limit. The total observable histogram estimator and public finite-sample interval attain this frontier, with resolution boundary \(\lambda_{\star}(n)=n^{-1/(4\beta+2)}\). For every fixed \(\beta_{\min}\in(1/4,1)\), honesty over the smoothness union \(\bigcup_{\gamma\in[\beta_{\min},1]}\mathcal P_\gamma\) forces expected length of rough-class order \(n^{-1/2}+\lambda^{2\beta_{\min}+1}\) already at the constant-regression, uniform-density baseline; constructing the interval at \(\beta_{\min}\) attains that order. Constants may depend on the fixed exponent. ACTIV-2 Day-3 viral RNA mediation motivates a prospective precision benchmark, without an assertion of class membership.
gap: Fully measured mediation theory supplies efficient estimation, while assay-censoring papers recover effects through modeling assumptions and coarsening theory studies analyst-chosen discretization. None of these results states what precision the deterministic assay experiment itself permits over a common smooth nonparametric class.
fill: The project supplies an explicit observable procedure with finite-sample coverage, a sharp equal-law assay modulus, a sampling lower bound, and the resulting root-\(n\) resolution boundary.
